_why: THE FAMILY PAGES: WHICH SURNAMES GET ONE, AND WHAT EACH IS ALLOWED TO SAY. Written 17 October 2026.
A family page here is about one SURNAME LINE: who bears it in this archive, where and when, and how it joins the
others. It is not the people index (/people/) and it is not a research page (/leibholz/, /wear-line/, /kurt/): it
is drawn from data this archive already holds and says nothing that data does not.
THE RULE FOR A CORE FAMILY. A surname is core if (1) a direct-line ancestor on the tree carries it, or (2) it has
at least eight published people, or (3) the work list names it in three or more row titles. Direct-line comes
first, then the number of published people who have died, then the number of work-list mentions; the first twelve
missing from the list are made. Twelve are made. Not made, and why, is in the report that came with this change,
not here: a reason written into a data file goes stale the day the next page is added.
WHAT IS DERIVED AT BUILD TIME (src/lib/families.js), NEVER TYPED HERE: the people, their years and places, the
marriages that join one family to another, the tree entries, the lanes (src/data/lines.json) and the counts. Nothing
in this file is a research claim. What is typed here is only a DECLARATION, in the way page-subjects.json is:
register / register_ids / english   which people the page counts (by surname, plus ids the surname misses);
tree                                which tree entries carry the name;
tree_links                          which people each tree entry is about, DECLARED rather than matched;
say                                 verbatim fragments of the tree's own wording for an entry;
notes                               a verbatim sentence from another page of this archive, with where it is from;
forms                               the spellings this archive already groups, with the page that groups them;
pages                               the pages of this archive that tell the family's story.
tools/check-families.py reads the built site and fails if a fragment is not verbatim in its source, a declared
person is not the one the tree entry names, a listed page does not mention the family, a living person appears,
or a family page is missing from the nav, the index or the sitemap. It is tested against planted faults.
THE LIVING STANDARD (version 2): a family page counts the living and names none of them. Their names, relationships
and place are on their own pages and on their relatives' pages, which is where the standard puts them; a family
page that listed them would make them easier to find than their own pages do.

notes.text: That is a collection of every Luwinski found in the German and Polish registers, parked under a placeholder so it could be kept. It is useful and worth keeping. It is not descent, and it is not presented here as though it were.
Not one of these people has been shown to connect to Joachim Luwinski of Allenstein.
Eight households of one surname, seven of them in one city and the eighth in Melbourne.
None of the seven is proved kin to Derrick's line
